action_trace.summary: Generated 10 structured interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (on-device deployment targets), pain points (export-lowering bottlenecks), and acceptance criteria (performance thresholds, model scope, graceful degradation). Questions decompose the e2e workflow into stakeholder, environment, and success-metric dimensions to ground requirements in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 practices.

Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (on-device performance targets), pain points (current workflow friction), and acceptance criteria (latency/memory bounds, model compatibility, diagnostic needs). Questions decompose the end-to-end transformer-to-ExecuTorch workflow into concrete user expectations and prioritization drivers.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (on-device deployment), pain points (current deployment friction), and acceptance criteria (performance thresholds, workflow validation points). Questions decompose the complex requirement into user context, technical constraints, success metrics, and operational workflows to ground subsequent requirements analysis.

End users require a unified, low-friction workflow for deploying HuggingFace transformer models to on-device targets via StaticCache and ExecuTorch. Core pain points are fragmented tooling, KV cache complexity, and performance tuning expertise gaps. The solution must deliver reasonable inference performance out-of-the-box while minimizing manual optimization steps.

End-users require a seamless, zero-friction pipeline for deploying HuggingFace transformers to on-device targets via StaticCache and ExecuTorch. Core blockers are fragmented tooling, KV cache inefficiency, and manual configuration complexity. Success criteria: <5 LOC integration, transparent StaticCache propagation, and production-ready latency/memory on edge hardware out-of-the-box.

End users require a seamless HuggingFace-to-ExecuTorch pipeline with StaticCache integration to eliminate manual optimization friction, reduce KV cache memory overhead by 80%+, and achieve 2-4ms per-token latency on mobile devices, enabling production-grade on-device transformer deployment without specialized expertise.

Clarification needed on performance baselines, StaticCache constraints (batch size flexibility), delegate prioritization, model scope (standard vs. custom), acceptable model size trade-offs, quantization integration, sequence length validation, and version compatibility to fully scope the end-to-end transformer deployment workflow.

Six clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in performance targets, StaticCache flexibility, delegate prioritization, optimization automation scope, developer experience model, and StaticCache injection mechanism. These address gaps between business expectations (e2e workflow, reasonable performance, minimal friction) and technical implementation details needed for requirements specification.

EndUser raises six clarification questions addressing ambiguous requirements: (1) quantified performance targets for 'reasonable out-of-the-box' performance across device classes, (2) StaticCache flexibility for variable batch/sequence sizes, (3) ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and fallback strategies, (4) handling variable sequence lengths in production inference, (5) tool integration contracts across HuggingFace-PyTorch-ExecuTorch pipeline, and (6) definition of 'minimal code changes' for developer experience. These questions bridge the gap between high-level business expectations and concrete technical implementation requirements.

End-user requirements for transformer on-device deployment workflow are validated as addressing real pain points. Four refinements needed: quantify 'reasonable performance' metrics by device class, clarify StaticCache sequence length handling strategy, prioritize ExecuTorch delegates with fallback logic, and define batch size flexibility constraints. Core e2e vision (HuggingFace→PyTorch→ExecuTorch) and StaticCache integration approach are confirmed as sound.

End-user validates core e2e workflow requirement but requires refinement on three fronts: (1) quantified performance baselines per device class, (2) StaticCache sequence length strategy for variable-length inference, (3) ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and fallback handling. Confirmations establish that workflow addresses critical deployment friction and KV cache efficiency gaps.

End-user confirms core e2e workflow requirement is valid and addresses deployment friction pain point. Three critical refinements needed: (1) quantify 'reasonable performance' with device-class-specific baselines, (2) clarify StaticCache handling of variable sequence lengths and batch sizes, (3) define ExecuTorch delegate scope and prioritization for initial release. These refinements will operationalize requirements and enable clear acceptance criteria.

Consolidated 6 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue following ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards. CONFIRMED: core e2e workflow requirement and StaticCache KV cache solution validity. REQUIRES REFINEMENT: quantified performance baselines per device class (mobile <100ms/<50MB, edge <50ms/<100MB), StaticCache sequence length strategy (fixed vs. multi-export), ExecuTorch delegate prioritization order, and batch size variability constraints. Chain-of-Thought analysis reveals 3 confirmed requirements, 3 refinement areas, and 0 showstoppers; ready for deployer validation phase.

Synthesized 9-item hierarchical user requirements list for transformers_2024q3 on-device deployment workflow. Core MUST requirements establish end-to-end pipeline (HuggingFace→StaticCache→ExecuTorch→device), quantified performance baselines per device class, and delegate prioritization strategy. SHOULD items address batch size variability and variable-length inference handling post-export. COULD items address tooling unification and reference models. All items traced to interview records (IR-001 through IR-006), confirmed pain points, and clarification questions; MoSCoW prioritization applied via life-cycle trade-off reasoning per BABOK v3 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148.

Nine targeted probes formulated to extract deployer-specific constraints on infrastructure (hardware targets, accelerator availability), security mandates (model encryption, compliance), scalability expectations (model size ranges, adaptive resource allocation), delegate prioritization (accelerator fallback strategy), sequence length handling (fixed vs. variable), performance baselines (hard vs. soft constraints), batch size flexibility, toolchain integration, and degradation strategies. These probes operationalize IR-002, IR-003, IR-004, IR-006 refinements and enable concrete deployment architecture decisions.

Eight targeted deployment-focused questions probing infrastructure constraints (device specs, OTA support, memory limits), security mandates (model IP, cache-timing), scalability expectations (dynamic delegate selection, memory budgeting), and critical ambiguities (sequence length rigidity, batch variability) to operationalize the e2e transformer workflow and quantified performance baselines (mobile <100ms/<50MB, edge <50ms/<100MB) across ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and StaticCache integration.

Formulated 10 targeted Deployer questions spanning infrastructure constraints (device specs, model size limits), security mandates (data residency, threat model), scalability expectations (multi-device support, model size ranges), performance validation (accuracy thresholds, benchmarking), and operational concerns (batch/sequence flexibility, OTA updates). Questions probe gaps in IR-002, IR-003, IR-004, and IR-006 to operationalize 'reasonable performance' and clarify StaticCache deployment trade-offs.

Deployer confirms infrastructure constraints (CPU-baseline mandatory with optional GPU/NPU/DSP delegates and graceful fallback), security mandates (export-time validation, model signature verification), scalability targets (fixed batch size 1-4 mobile / 1-8 edge, delegate prioritization chain), and operational procedures (6-step deployment checklist, performance validation gates, StaticCache configuration documentation, cost-performance trade-off quantification). Mobile/edge performance baselines <100ms/<50MB and <50ms/<100MB enforced as deployment gates.

Deployer constraints establish CPU-baseline ExecuTorch execution with quantified latency/memory targets (mobile <100ms/<50MB, edge <50ms/<100MB), mandate StaticCache pre-allocation at export time for memory safety and attack prevention, enforce immutable signed model artifacts, and operationalize variable batch size via multi-export pattern; delegate prioritization (CPU→GPU→NPU→DSP) with automatic fallback ensures scalability across heterogeneous hardware while cost optimization via fixed-shape KV cache reduces deployment footprint 15-30%.

Deployer confirms infrastructure constraints (CPU-baseline mandatory, mobile <100ms/<50MB, edge <50ms/<100MB), StaticCache memory pre-allocation at export time, security validation of cache configuration, multi-tier delegate prioritization with CPU fallback, and operational procedures for end-to-end workflow validation. Clarification needed on batch size variability post-export and multi-export strategy for variable-length inference scenarios.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications blocking operational deployment: (1) sequence length flexibility strategy post-export for variable-length inference, (2) batch size variability support and configuration methodology, (3) ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and fallback chain for heterogeneous targets, (4) operationalization of performance baselines across reference device sets with measurement methodology, and (5) StaticCache validation, signing, and immutability guarantees for security compliance. These clarifications are prerequisite for defining concrete system requirements and deployment architecture.

Six critical clarifications required to operationalize the end-to-end transformer deployment workflow: (1) sequence length flexibility strategy post-export, (2) batch size variability constraints at inference, (3) ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and fallback chain, (4) performance baseline operationalization methodology, (5) export-time validation and security enforcement, and (6) MVP scope decision between single-export simplicity vs. multi-export flexibility. These clarifications directly impact infrastructure constraints, memory guarantees, and deployment flexibility across mobile and edge device classes.

Six clarification questions raised on critical operational unknowns: (1) sequence length flexibility strategy post-export, (2) batch size variability at inference time, (3) ExecuTorch delegate prioritization and fallback chain, (4) performance baseline binding (hard requirement vs. aspirational), (5) StaticCache dtype handling automation, (6) multi-export workflow complexity and MVP scope. These clarifications are prerequisite to operationalizing StaticCache integration across export/lowering stages and defining measurable acceptance criteria per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deploy environment standards.

Deployer validates and refines 6 critical deployment requirements: (1) end-to-end workflow feasible with CPU-baseline + optional delegates, (2) sequence length fixed at export to guarantee memory bounds, (3) batch size immutable post-export for latency predictability, (4) performance baselines operationalized per device class with validation gates, (5) delegate fallback chain prioritized (CPU→GPU→NPU/DSP), (6) export-time security validation prevents runtime memory attacks. All refinements lock deployment-critical decisions while maintaining infrastructure feasibility and addressing user pain points.

Deployer confirms end-to-end transformer workflow is deployment-feasible. Locked decisions: (1) fixed sequence length + batch size at StaticCache export time for memory safety; (2) quantified performance baselines per device class; (3) mandatory CPU baseline with optional GPU/NPU/DSP delegates and graceful fallback; (4) export-time validation of StaticCache config. Phase 1 scope: single fixed-length export with CPU baseline. Variable-length and advanced delegate scenarios deferred to Phase 2.

Deployer confirms end-to-end transformer workflow (HuggingFace → PyTorch StaticCache → ExecuTorch → on-device) is deployment-feasible with infrastructure constraints locked: CPU-baseline mandatory, fixed sequence/batch size at export time, quantified performance baselines per device class (Mobile: <100ms/<50MB, Edge: <50ms/<100MB), delegate prioritization chain (CPU→GPU→NPU/DSP), and security validation at export. Multi-length/batch flexibility deferred post-GA. All clarifications resolved; ready for implementation.

Operating environment specification for transformer on-device deployment workflow: CPU-baseline ExecuTorch execution mandatory across mobile (<100ms, <50MB) and edge (<50ms, <100MB) targets; StaticCache requires fixed sequence length and batch size at export time for deterministic memory allocation; GPU/NPU/DSP delegates optional with graceful CPU fallback; export-time validation prevents runtime memory exhaustion; offline workflow from HuggingFace → PyTorch → ExecuTorch with immutable exported models; multi-device scalability via delegate prioritization chain.

All six review findings resolved via SRS revisions: clarity violations addressed through precise API/configuration specifications; verifiability violations closed via quantified test conditions per device class; feasibility conflict resolved by aligning automatic cache management with fixed-length export constraint; traceability gaps filled with explicit delegate prioritization and device-class mappings; consistency violations reconciled by documenting single-export strategy for initial release; and immutability/validation requirements formalized per deployer security mandates. SRS now ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148-compliant and deployment-feasible.
